Subject: KMS design for private deployment — remote signing proxy & operator authz

Hi Logan / Soojin / Marissa,

Thanks again for the architecture walkthrough earlier. As discussed, AcmeCloud is moving forward with a private Redwood deployment in our VPC and we need to finalize KMS and HSM controls for the go-live. Attached is a draft topology (acme-proposed-kms-topology.png) and a short operator matrix.

High-level asks from our security team:
- We need BYOK with vendor-provided HSM attestation and must support remote signing from our application layer (no plaintext key material on host).
- Operator separation: Acme will require a granular operator RBAC matrix (who can unseal, who can rotate KEKs, who can request signing).
- Rotation cadence expectations and emergency unseal/eviction playbook — regulators want explicit steps and audit traces.
- Network egress constraints: HSM attestation and CRL lookups only, deny all other outbound by default.

Can you confirm Redwood's recommended pattern for a remote signing proxy (signing requests leave the application but never expose private keys) and how operator service accounts are intended to be scoped? Also please call out where we should expect audit events and recommended retention windows.

We’ve penciled a short compliance review for next Friday; if we can align on answers and a small design doc before then that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Elaine
Elaine Park
Director, Cloud Security — AcmeCloud Inc.

Elaine — thanks, this is clear and helpful. Quick summary / what we propose for the items you listed: 

1) Remote signing proxy model:
- Host an authorized signing proxy inside the customer VPC (as a managed Redwood appliance or container) that communicates with an HSM (FIPS-level) over an internal network. The application calls the proxy over mTLS; the proxy holds only a short-lived wrapping key and forwards signing operations to the HSM (keys never leave the device).
- Support both PKCS#11 and a JSON-RPC signing API so customers can choose integration path.

2) Operator service accounts & RBAC:
- We recommend three operator roles: Operator-Admin (can manage cluster/network/patching), Key-Admin (create/rotate KEK, define key policies), and Audit-Only (read-only access to telemetry/logs).
- Each role is tied to a unique service account and must use client cert MFA for HSM operations. We will provide a responsibility matrix (see attached spreadsheet) you can customize for Acme.

3) Rotation & emergency unseal:
- Default rotation cadence: data keys rotated every 90 days; KEKs rotated every 12 months (or on-demand). We support canary rollouts for KEK rotation to avoid rewrap storms.
- Emergency unseal: dual-control process requiring two Key-Admin approvals via Docusign/approval webhook; we can include an offline split secret escrow if regulators require. Full steps and required audit events are included in our playbook.

4) Audit events & retention:
- Signing request logs, key lifecycle events (create/rotate/destroy), operator auth events, attestation results are emitted to the local syslog/CloudWatch-forwarder and to the private control-plane audit store. Default retention is 13 months; we can extend per contract.

5) Network & egress:
- HSM attestation and CRL/OCSP are expected egress; everything else can be whitelisted. The signing proxy uses ephemeral outbound for kernel metrics only; we can architect to avoid all outbound if needed.

Next steps: Soojin will propose an operator-level network ACL and a minimal RFC for the signing proxy interface. Can we do a short call Thursday 10am PT? I’ll attach the filled operator matrix.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Thanks Logan / Elaine — notes from the implementation POV below. I’ve attached a draft operator responsibility matrix and a small network diagram to show the proposed segmentation.

Implementation specifics (concise):
- HSM/KEK topology: Customer HSM cluster (active/passive) in a private subnet. KEK is a wrap-only asymmetric key stored in HSM. Data keys are CEPH-style envelope-wrapped by KEK.
- Attestation & identity: HSM will provide hardware attestation (chip cert). Signing proxy will present a VM mTLS client cert signed by Acme CA; HSM will verify the proxy certificate before allowing PKCS#11 operations.
- Service accounts & authz: Each Redwood operator identity is a short-lived kubernetes service account certificate tied to an operator SSO identity. KMS operations require an additional HSM-level approval token (2-of-3 operators or 1 operator + emergency delegate).
- Audit surface:
  * PKCS#11 session open/close (partial payload hash)
  * Sign/Decrypt operation id (no plaintext)
  * KEK lifecycle events (create/rotate/wrap)
  * Operator approval/eviction events
- Retention/forwarding: We will forward telemetry to an Acme-managed log collector. Default local retention is 90 days; control-plane audit store 13 months. We can ship an extended retention option as part of the Dedicated contract.
- Egress hardening: Only outbound endpoints allowed: HSM vendor attestation endpoint, OCSP/CRL, and the Redwood control-plane telemetry endpoint (TLS). Support for a proxy-bastion for all external calls.

Emergency unseal & operator eviction playbook (short):
1) Operator identifies incident -> create incident ticket (Jira ID)
2) Two Key-Admin approvals via Docusign/approval webhook to issue an ephemeral unseal token
3) Use unseal token to mount KEK and rewrap impacted data keys
4) Rotate KEK if compromise suspected; run an automated rewrap job with canary traffic to validate
5) Full audit export to Acme audit bucket and a forensic snapshot of HSM attestation logs

I’ll have a full RFC for the signing proxy interface (JSON-RPC + PKCS#11 mapping) by end of day. For Thursday’s call I recommend inviting your infra security lead to walk the ACLs.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
